title: Structure Decisions and Actions
lede: Use this prompt to turn raw meeting notes into a clean, structured record. MossAIc extracts decisions, owners, due dates, risks, open questions, and follow-ups — so nothing falls through the cracks after the meeting ends.

steps.title: Capture your notes
steps.text: During or after the meeting, jot down notes in whatever format works — bullet points, free text, or even a transcript.

steps.title: Remove confidential details
steps.text: Before pasting into MossAIc, redact any sensitive information (personal data, financials, NDA-covered content).

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the prompt below into MossAIc along with your meeting notes.

steps.title: Distribute the output
steps.text: Review the structured output, make corrections, and share with attendees for confirmation.

prompt:
You are an experienced Business Analyst processing meeting notes.

Meeting notes:
[Paste your raw meeting notes here]

Extract and organize the following into a clean, structured format:

1. **Decisions Made** — Each decision with a brief rationale
2. **Action Items** — Each with: description, owner, due date (or "TBD" if not stated)
3. **Risks Identified** — Any risks, concerns, or blockers mentioned
4. **Open Questions** — Unresolved items that need follow-up
5. **Parking Lot** — Topics raised but deferred to a future discussion
6. **Key Discussion Points** — Brief summary of major topics covered

Use a table for action items. Flag any decisions that seem to lack an owner or where the notes are ambiguous.
whenToUse: You have rough meeting notes and need to extract clear outcomes
You want to ensure every decision has an owner and due date
You need to surface risks, open questions, and follow-ups quickly
proTips: Run this immediately after the meeting while context is fresh
If using a transcript, trim filler and off-topic sections first for cleaner results
Pair with your team's standard meeting-minutes template for consistency
remember: Always remove confidential details before prompting. Review every AI output — you own the final deliverable.

title: Build an Interview Guide
lede: Use this prompt to turn a discovery objective into a focused, well-sequenced stakeholder interview guide. It produces open questions grouped by theme so you can uncover goals, pain points, decisions, and success measures without leading the interviewee.

steps.title: Define your objective
steps.text: Write a clear one-sentence discovery goal. Example: “Understand how the field team currently tracks equipment inspections and where the process breaks down.”

steps.title: List what you already know
steps.text: Note any context — systems involved, team names, known pain points — so the prompt can tailor questions rather than repeat obvious ground.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the prompt below into MossAIc, fill in the bracketed placeholders, and submit.

steps.title: Review & refine
steps.text: Check the generated questions. Remove duplicates, reorder for conversation flow, and add follow-ups specific to your stakeholder.

prompt:
You are an experienced Business Analyst preparing for a stakeholder interview.

Objective: [Describe the discovery goal in one sentence]
Context: [List known systems, teams, pain points, or constraints]
Stakeholder role: [Title and area of responsibility]

Generate a structured interview guide with:
1. Opening questions (rapport and role context)
2. Current-state questions (process, tools, data)
3. Pain-point questions (friction, workarounds, risks)
4. Future-state questions (goals, success measures, priorities)
5. Closing questions (anything missed, next steps)

Use open-ended questions. Avoid leading or yes/no questions. Group by theme and include 3-5 questions per section.
whenToUse: You are preparing for a stakeholder interview and need focused questions
You want to ensure consistent coverage across multiple interviews
You need to uncover goals, pain points, and success measures systematically
proTips: Swap in the stakeholder's actual title for more relevant questions
Run it once per stakeholder role to create tailored guides
After the interview, paste your notes back into MossAIc and ask it to extract key themes
remember: Always remove confidential details before prompting. Review every AI output — you own the final deliverable.

title: Challenge Requirement Quality
lede: Use this prompt as a second set of eyes on a draft requirement or user story. MossAIc checks for ambiguity, testability, hidden assumptions, and missing edge cases — helping you strengthen the requirement before it reaches development.

steps.title: Draft your requirement
steps.text: Write the requirement or user story in your usual format. Include acceptance criteria if you have them.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the prompt below into MossAIc with your draft requirement in the placeholder.

steps.title: Review the analysis
steps.text: MossAIc will flag issues across several quality dimensions. Not every flag will apply — use your judgment.

steps.title: Revise and re-check
steps.text: Update the requirement based on valid flags, then optionally re-run for a second pass.

prompt:
You are a senior Business Analyst reviewing a draft requirement for quality.

Requirement:
[Paste the full requirement or user story here, including any acceptance criteria]

Analyze this requirement against these quality dimensions:
1. **Clarity** — Is the language unambiguous? Flag vague terms (e.g., "quickly", "user-friendly", "appropriate").
2. **Completeness** — Are there missing details, undefined actors, or unspecified triggers?
3. **Testability** — Can each statement be verified with a concrete test? Suggest test conditions where missing.
4. **Assumptions** — What hidden assumptions does this requirement make? List them explicitly.
5. **Edge cases** — What boundary conditions, error states, or exception paths are not addressed?
6. **Conflicts** — Does anything contradict common patterns or other stated criteria?

For each issue found, state the problem, quote the problematic text, and suggest a specific revision.
whenToUse: You have drafted requirements and want a quality check before review
You need to catch ambiguity, assumptions, and missing edge cases
You want to verify requirements are testable and measurable
proTips: Batch multiple requirements in one prompt for efficiency
Use the output as a discussion starter with your product owner, not as a final verdict
Re-run after revisions to confirm the flags are resolved
remember: Always remove confidential details before prompting. Review every AI output — you own the final deliverable.
